name: LM555CN_NOPB
title: LM555 timer: bipolar 555 for delays and oscillation, PDIP, SOIC and VSSOP
summary: The LM555 is the bipolar 555 timer, a pin-for-pin replacement for the SE555 and NE555. As a one-shot one resistor and one capacitor set the pulse width (1.1 RC); as an oscillator two resistors and one capacitor set frequency and duty cycle, with timing from microseconds to hours and a result that does not move with the supply. The output sources or sinks up to 200 mA. It runs from 4.5 V to 16 V over 0 °C to 70 °C; LM555CN/NOPB is the 8-pin PDIP part.
key_figures: 4.5 V to 16 V (18 V max recommended)
3 mA typ at 5 V, 10 mA typ at 15 V with the output low, no load

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground; every voltage of the part is measured from it.

pins.name: TRIGGER
pins.function: Trigger input of the lower comparator. Pulling it below 1/3 VCC sets the flip-flop, which drives the output high and releases the timing capacitor.

pins.name: OUTPUT
pins.function: Timer output. It can source or sink up to 200 mA and drive TTL.

pins.name: RESET
pins.function: Active-low reset. A low pulse on this pin stops or restarts the timing and forces the output low. Tie it to VCC when it is not used, so noise cannot cause a false trigger.

pins.name: CONTROL VOLTAGE
pins.function: Gives access to the internal divider that sets the threshold and trigger levels, and so the output pulse width. A voltage forced onto the pin modulates the output; the circuits bypass it with 0.01 µF.

pins.name: THRESHOLD
pins.function: Input of the upper comparator, whose reference is 2/3 VCC. Reaching that level resets the flip-flop and the output goes low.

pins.name: DISCHARGE
pins.function: Open-collector transistor to GND that empties the timing capacitor between intervals. It switches in step with the output: on while the output is low.

circuits.title: Monostable (one-shot)
circuits.description: A one-shot timer. Between pulses the discharge transistor holds C empty and the output sits low. A negative-going pulse on TRIGGER below 1/3 VCC sets the flip-flop: the output goes high and C charges from VCC through RA. When C reaches 2/3 VCC at THRESHOLD the flip-flop resets, DISCHARGE empties C and the output returns low, so the output pulse lasts 1.1 RA C whatever the supply between +5 V and +15 V. CONTROL VOLTAGE is bypassed with 0.01 µF. The output serves a load wired to VCC (on while the timer is idle) or a load wired to ground (on during the pulse). RESET is brought out and may be tied to VCC.
notes: RESET has an optional link to VCC.
The two loads are alternatives; either or both may be fitted.

circuits.title: Astable (free-running oscillator)
circuits.description: A free-running oscillator. TRIGGER and THRESHOLD are joined on the timing capacitor, so the timer retriggers itself. C charges from VCC through RA and RB in series and discharges through RB alone into DISCHARGE, swinging between 1/3 VCC and 2/3 VCC. The output is high for 0.693 (RA + RB) C and low for 0.693 RB C, giving f = 1.44 / ((RA + 2RB) C), independent of the supply; the ratio of RA to RB sets the duty cycle. RESET is tied to VCC and CONTROL VOLTAGE is bypassed with 0.01 µF. The output drives a load to VCC or a load to ground.
notes: The two loads are alternatives; either or both may be fitted.

circuits.title: Monostable LED flasher with pushbutton trigger
circuits.description: A one-shot that lights an LED for about five seconds each time a button is pressed. The button pulls TRIGGER to ground against a 10 kΩ pull-up to VCC, which starts the timing: the output goes high and lights the LED through 470 Ω, while the 470 µF timing capacitor charges through 10 kΩ. When it reaches 2/3 VCC the output drops and DISCHARGE empties the capacitor. The delay is t = 1.1 R C. RESET is unused and tied to VCC; CONTROL VOLTAGE is bypassed with 0.01 µF. The supply is +5 V to +15 V.
notes: The design procedure aims at a 5 s delay: RC = 4.545 s, so R = 100 kΩ calls for C = 45.4 µF, and standard values of 100 kΩ and 47 µF are chosen. The circuit values of 10 kΩ and 470 µF give the same RC product. The measured delay is 5.17 s.
RESET has a link to VCC.

operation.text: A bipolar timer for accurate delays and oscillation, pin-compatible with the SE555 and NE555 so it drops into their footprints unchanged. One resistor and one capacitor fix a delay; two resistors and one capacitor fix the frequency and duty cycle of an oscillator. Timing runs from microseconds to hours. Trigger and reset act on falling edges, and the output sources or sinks up to 200 mA or drives TTL. Temperature stability is better than 0.005 % per °C. Packages are 8-pin PDIP, SOIC and VSSOP.

Replaces the SE555 and NE555 directly. Timing from microseconds to hours. Runs astable or monostable, with adjustable duty cycle. Output sources or sinks 200 mA; output and supply are TTL compatible. Temperature stability better than 0.005 % per °C. Normally-on and normally-off outputs. Offered in an 8-pin VSSOP as well as PDIP and SOIC.
Precision timing; Pulse generation; Sequential timing; Time delay generation; Pulse width modulation (PWM); Pulse position modulation (PPM); Linear ramps.

As a one-shot, an internal transistor keeps the external capacitor discharged until a negative pulse below 1/3 VCC reaches pin 2. That sets the flip-flop, which removes the short across the capacitor and takes the output high. The capacitor then charges exponentially for t = 1.1 RA C, reaching 2/3 VCC, when the comparator resets the flip-flop, discharges the capacitor and returns the output low. Because both the charging and the comparator threshold scale with the supply, the interval does not depend on it. A larger or smaller R or C lengthens or shortens the pulse.

While the output is high, further trigger pulses have no effect, provided the trigger input has gone back high at least 10 µs before the interval ends. A negative pulse on RESET (pin 4) ends the interval early, and the output then stays low until the next trigger. With reset unused, RESET is connected to VCC to guard against false triggering.

With pins 2 and 6 joined, the timer triggers itself and runs as a multivibrator. Charging runs through RA + RB and discharging through RB only, the capacitor moving between 1/3 VCC and 2/3 VCC; the ratio of the two resistors sets the duty cycle. As in the one-shot, neither the charging nor the discharging time, nor therefore the frequency, depends on the supply.
Set to a suitable timing-cycle length, the monostable circuit works as a frequency divider. The waveforms show it dividing by three.

When pin 2 is pulled fully to ground the lower comparator's storage time can reach 10 µs, which sets a 10 µs minimum monostable pulse width. Reset-to-output delay is 0.47 µs typical and the reset pulse must be at least 0.3 µs wide, typical. The discharge (pin 7) current follows the output (pin 3) voltage to within 30 ns.

The most common use is the one-shot; the example lights an LED for a set time after a pushbutton pulls the trigger pin low. The design target is a 5 s delay, which with t = 1.1 R C makes RC = 4.545 s. With R = 100 kΩ, C comes to 45.4 µF, and the standard values 100 kΩ and 47 µF are used. The momentary button to ground has a 10 kΩ pull-up to the supply; the LED and a series resistor run from the output to ground; reset goes to the supply. Built and measured, the delay is 5.17 s: the output rises as the trigger pulses low and the capacitor starts charging, and falls when the capacitor reaches 2/3 of the supply.
The supply must be within 4.5 V to 16 V. Bypassing protects the surrounding circuits: at least 0.1 µF in parallel with a 1 µF electrolytic, placed as near the LM555 as possible on short traces.

Ordinary board rules apply. The 0.1 µF and 1 µF electrolytic bypass pair sits as close to the timer as possible, and the timing capacitor close to the discharge pin. A bottom-layer ground plane improves noise immunity and signal integrity. The layout example places C1 (timing capacitor, from the delay calculation), C2 (0.01 µF bypass on the control voltage pin), C3 (0.1 µF ceramic bypass), C4 (1 µF electrolytic bypass) and R1 (timing resistor, from the delay calculation).
ESD protection is limited: store and handle the parts with leads shorted together or in conductive foam.
